system.description:
“But everybody has to sometimes break the rules”

Cheats are the underdogs of society: They were not trained in elite academies, they were not born with psionic powers, and they often lack the connections or backing that others take for granted. Nethertheless Cheats are always coming out on top. They just don’t play fair. That’s not their game. They use everything they have to turn the tables: Tech, deception, diversion, their own cleverness… and sometimes just dumb luck. In the end no one’s asking how the job was done. What counts is that it was paid.

attribution.source: The New Unknown Playtest v2.0 Mind

backgroundQuestions: Who taught you your first trick — and what betrayal made you stop trusting them?
You pulled off a con that spiraled out of control. What happened — and why do people still whisper about it?
What system or law did you learn to bend so well that it became second nature?
Whose trust did you shatter with one of your scams — and what excuse do you still use to justify it?
What's the one rule you swore you'd never break — and how close are you to crossing that line?
connections: You once covered for me when a scheme went sideways. What did it cost you — and why didn't you sell me out?
I slipped you an edge at the perfect moment. What was it, and why do you still carry it?
You've seen me cheat when no one else noticed. Why did you keep it to yourself?
I owe you for a risk you took on my behalf. Why haven't you called in that debt?
You know the one secret that could ruin me. Why haven't you used it against me?
